catalog_quote: Le Kinyindu est une langue bantu. Par ailleurs, il s’agit d’une langue à tons et il n’y est pas facile de prononcer un mot correctement sans recourir à un ton approprié et c’est ce ton qui confère le sens au mot. new_statements.translation: Kinyindu is a Bantu language. Moreover, it is a tone language and it is not easy to pronounce a word correctly without using the appropriate tone, and it is this tone that gives the word its meaning. The rise or fall of the voice in speech affects the meaning of what is said.

Par ailleurs, il s’agit d’une langue à tons et il n’y est pas facile de prononcer un mot correctement sans recourir à un ton approprié et c’est ce ton qui confère le sens au mot. La montée ou la chute de la voix dans la parole affecte le sens de ce qui est dit." The second locator also checks: lines ~1200-1210 (printed p.25, heading 'Précision Linguistique') repeats it with scanned/copy variants ("langue en Tons", "confère les sens"), attributed to "Musombwa Ivuzi Michel", footnote 'MUSOMBWA IGUNZI Michel Ndahashuba Archives Le kinyindu page1'; footnote 15 (line 449)…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Only that Kinyindu has lexically distinctive tone; no statement anywhere in the accessible material about word stress/accent or penultimate prominence. (The SIL alphabet primer additionally shows contrastive vowel length written aa/ee/ii/oo/uu.)
new_statements.domain_note: Community-authored sociolinguistic fiche, not a linguistic description; statement concerns lexical tone at word level. No accessible source addresses stress; the only grammar sketch (Ruhekenya 1988) and the only phonology paper (Wikaliza 2005, ISP Bukavu) are unpublished and offline.
new_statements.identity_note: All accessible material concerns Kinyindu of the Luindi (Lwindi) chefferie, Mwenga territory, Sud-Kivu (Kasika–Kigogo–Ilangi triangle) = Glottolog nyin1248 / ISO nyg, Guthrie JD501. Glottolog 5.x places it in a Fuliiric node with Fuliiru (fuli1240); Ethnologue reports 90% lexical similarity Fuliiru–Nyindu and describes Nyindu speech as 'a mixture of Lega-Mwenga and Shi'. Any statement taken from Van Otterloo 2011 would be about Fuliiru, not Nyindu, and must be flagged as a proxy.

sources.note: Section 'Précisions linguistiques': Kinyindu is a Bantu tone language, tone distinguishes word meanings; nothing on accent/stress. Bibliography names unpublished ISP-Bukavu papers (Wikaliza 2005 'A glimpse at Kinyindu phonology'; Kikitumaini 1999; Betu 2001).

sources.note: OLAC: only Glottolog and Ethnologue entries; Ethnologue: classification JD501, 'speech reportedly a mixture of Lega-Mwenga and Shi'; Glottolog title search adds only Yamada 1999 and Igunzi 2013.
